court: Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

issues.label: MCA jurisdiction over Indian defendant
issues.why: The court must confirm federal jurisdiction over Mr. Smith's offenses under the Major Crimes Act because he is Indian and offenses occurred in Indian country.

issues.label: GCA/ACA jurisdiction over non-Indian defendant
issues.why: The court must confirm jurisdiction over Mrs. Smith under the General Crimes Act and Assimilative Crimes Act as a non-Indian who harmed an Indian victim.

issues.label: Castro-Huerta effect on federal jurisdiction
issues.why: Mrs. Smith argues Castro-Huerta deprives the federal court of subject-matter jurisdiction over her offenses.

issues.label: Concurrent state jurisdiction not exclusivity
issues.why: Castro-Huerta held states have concurrent jurisdiction, which may not divest federal jurisdiction, so the court must assess its actual holding.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction non-waivability
issues.why: Jurisdictional challenges can be raised at any time and cannot be forfeited, affecting timeliness of Mrs. Smith's arguments.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting Mr. Smith under GCA
issues.why: Mr. Smith argues an Indian cannot be convicted of aiding and abetting under the GCA for Indian-on-Indian offenses.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting Mrs. Smith under MCA
issues.why: Mrs. Smith argues the MCA applies only to Indian defendants and cannot support prosecuting her as aider or abettor.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting jurisdictional theory
issues.why: The court must determine each defendant's principal liability independently of aiding-and-abetting so jurisdiction stands regardless.

issues.label: Preservation of aiding-and-abetting objection
issues.why: The court must decide whether the objection was properly preserved and the applicable standard of review.

issues.label: Analogous guideline determination
issues.why: The court must decide whether a sufficiently analogous guideline exists for Oklahoma child abuse under U.S.S.G. § 2X5.1.

issues.label: Applicability of §2A2.2 aggravated assault
issues.why: Mr. Smith argues the aggravated assault guideline is the most analogous starting point for his child abuse conviction.

issues.label: §3553 default when no analogous guideline
issues.why: If no sufficiently analogous guideline exists, sentencing proceeds directly under 18 U.S.C. § 3553 with statutory maximum ceiling.

issues.label: Statutory maximum for assimilated/MCA offense
issues.why: The court must confirm the applicable statutory maximum penalty, whether up to life, for the underlying Oklahoma offenses.

issues.label: Procedural reasonableness of sentence
issues.why: Mr. Smith challenges the sentence as procedurally unreasonable due to guideline miscalculation.

issues.label: Substantive reasonableness of sentences
issues.why: The court must assess whether the 180- and 240-month sentences are substantively reasonable under §3553(a).

issues.label: Victim status under §3771(e)(2)
issues.why: The court must determine whether the letter authors qualify as victims entitled to submit impact statements.

issues.label: Adequacy of notice/time for letters
issues.why: Defendants argue 22 hours was insufficient to review victim-impact letters submitted before sentencing.

issues.label: Whether letters affected the sentence
issues.why: Any error in considering the letters must be assessed for prejudice or harmlessness.

issues.label: Timeliness of second post-trial motion
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mrs. Smith's second Rule 29/33 motion was filed within applicable deadlines.

issues.label: Rule 33 timing and jurisdictional nature
issues.why: The court must consider whether Rule 33/29 deadlines are jurisdictional or claim-processing and whether excusable.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence for convictions
issues.why: Rule 29 requires assessing whether evidence supports child abuse and neglect convictions against each defendant.

issues.label: Assimilation of Oklahoma statute elements
issues.why: The court must ensure the Oklahoma offense elements are properly incorporated and satisfied under the ACA.

issues.label: Victim identity consistency
issues.why: The victim was identified by multiple names (H.M., M.V., K.B.), which may bear on evidentiary and jurisdictional proof.

issues.label: Mrs. Smith's medical-needs defense
issues.why: The court must weigh whether the government disproved the defense that H.M.'s condition reflected medical needs.
